1.he: לְאֶרֶץ עַזָּה. אַחֲרֵי יְגִיעָה קָשָׁה וְעַזָּה
1.note: Rhyme on עַזָּה: "Gaza" in the first line, "fierce" in the second.

2.note: The words "to the domain of its Owner" are in square brackets in the edition, an editor's addition.

3.note: "Eternal" (הָעוֹלָמִית, also "of the world") is in square brackets in the edition, an editor's addition.

4.note: יְחִידָתִי, "my only one", is the soul, as in Ps 22:21 and 35:17. So also in the next lines.

5.note: Play on the root אלם: "sheaves", "I have bound (sheaves)" (Gen 37:7) and "I am dumb".

6.note: Sound play: זְמָרָיו "its songs", נְמֵרָיו "its leopards", after מְתוּקָיו כְּמָרָיו "its sweet things like its bitter things".

7.note: Literally "will exchange its height for its pride"; the rhyme word גֵּאוֹ repeats the end of the line before. The sense is uncertain: perhaps that a day's events bring the proud low.

8.note: Pun: בַּצּוּרוֹת "in the rocks" (Job 28:10), בַּצּוֹרוֹת "in droughts" (compare Jer 14:1). The subject of this passage ("he") is not clear: the sinner who weeps, or Time.

10.note: The rhyme word תַּאֲוַתְכֶם ends three lines. Here it is read as "your bounds" (from תאה, "to mark out", Num 34:10); in the lines before and after it is "your lust" and "your desire". Uncertain.

11.note: Pun: אֳנִי "a fleet" (eyes as ships on a sea of tears), and אֲנִי "mourn" (imperative, from אנה, Isa 3:26).

12.note: חָרוּץ ends four lines: "sharp" (Isa 41:15), "decreed" (Isa 10:22), and here "gold" (Ps 68:14) or "diligence". Read as gold: riches do not help at death.

13.note: Pun: the first וְנָצוּ "and they lie waste" (from נצה, Jer 4:7), the second "and they have fled" (Lam 4:15). "Put on its armor" (כֵּלָיו עָדָה) is uncertain: עָדָה can also mean "passed".

14.note: Puah and Shiphrah are the Hebrew midwives of Exod 1:15. שִׁפְרָה also echoes שִׁפְרָה "made fair" (Job 26:13) at the end of the line before.

15.note: Pun: the first וְתַעַל "and You brought up", the second "cure" (תְּעָלָה, Jer 30:13). The thought is that God makes the cure before the wound (compare b. Megillah 13b).

16.note: Play on חלף: "they passed" and מַחְלְפוֹת "locks of hair" (Judg 16:13), perhaps the hair of youth. Uncertain.

17.note: Three words from the same letters: סַלּוֹנַי "my briers" (Ezek 2:6), סִלּוּנִי "they heaped me up" (or "exalted me"), סָלוּנִי "they trampled me" (Lam 1:15). The sense is uncertain.

18.note: מְרוּקָיו twice: "its perfumes" (Esth 2:12) and "its scourings". Likewise in the next two lines מְצוּקָיו is "its straits" and "its pillars" (1 Sam 2:8).

19.note: Uncertain. Perhaps the waters covered him, and his arrows (his defenses) were turned away from its riverbeds.

20.note: The same word ends both lines. Read first as "loathe" (from קוץ) and then as "rouse". "My prayer" renders שִׂיחַי, "my speech, my meditation".

21.note: הוֹדוֹ "its splendor" ends the line before too; here it is read as "cast" (from ידה). Uncertain.

22.he: וְזָרַק עָלָיו וּמְלֶאכֶת שִׂכְלִי נְמִבְזָה וְעָיְפוּ נַהֲלָאָיו וְעָלָיו עֹל וְהָפַךְ הַזְּמַן שַׁלְוִי לְפִיד
22.note: This line seems corrupt in the source (word order and forms such as נְמִבְזָה); the rendering is a guess. לְפִיד "into ruin" (Job 12:5) rhymes with לַפִּיד "a torch" in the next line.

23.note: נָשׁוּנִי twice: "they beguiled me" (from נשא, Gen 3:13) and "they forgot me" (from נשה, Gen 41:51). Uncertain.

25.note: Pun: the first וְתַעַזְבִי "and forsake", the second "and restore" (עזב as "repair", Neh 3:8).

26.note: Pun: זִיקֵךְ "your spark" (Isa 50:11) and "your fetters" (זִקִּים, Jer 40:1).

27.note: Pun on the name חֶבֶר (Ḥever) and מְחַבֵּר "composer"; also אֲחַבֵּר "I compose" in the next line.
